html:
SMTO-EXE-0132 — SMTO stopped a web browser step from running twice

GUID: 1717fbed-8de2-5c64-a1ca-fbedab4beecc
Slug: browser-duplicate
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO tried to send a browser step the Gateway had already received, so the Gateway refused to run it again. The first attempt may already have clicked, typed or submitted something.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation to look at the current page and tell you what it shows. The first attempt may have finished, and a fresh look shows whether the click or form already went through.
  2. If the page shows the step is done, continue from there. If it clearly didn't happen, ask SMTO to do it as a new step. A new request is accepted normally, and checking first stops the same action from happening twice.
  3. If this message appears again, open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. The details show which browser step was sent twice, so the person managing SMTO can find out why it was resent.

What success looks like

  • SMTO confirms the page shows the result you wanted, with the action done only once.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to repeat a purchase, payment or form submission until you've confirmed on the website that the first attempt didn't go through.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • BrowserService.execute refused dispatch because the execution ID is already active or recorded as finished in this Gateway service lifetime; for non-read operations the earlier effect remains unknown.

What this means

  • Browser admission found the execution ID already active or retained as finished and refused another dispatch; possible mutation effects remain marked unknown. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • Browser admission found the execution ID already active or retained as finished and refused another dispatch; possible mutation effects remain marked unknown.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original receipt and same-session page/download state with a separately authorized read if needed.

How to fix it

  • Do not resend the same execution_id. Establish the original outcome with a new read operation (browser.page_info, browser.snapshot or browser.downloads), then send any further mutation as a new operation with a new execution ID; check the Server log for why the ID was dispatched again (for example a resumed or replayed tool call).
  • Do not replay this execution. Reconcile existing page/session/download state using a new read operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Do not replay this execution. Reconcile existing page/session/download state using a new read operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The original effect is settled before any distinct new mutation is requested.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
